messages:
Emma: FYI customer ACME reporting sudden 502s from hosted API when doing streaming responses, started ~09:10 UTC. Spike only for their tenant, affects long-lived chat streams (~6-12s). sample trace id: t-acme-42. They say it started after config push earlier this morning.
Raj: Can you paste a quick repro curl or client snippet? Any common headers?
Emma: Repro with curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream\" -d '{"model":"x-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"long prompt..."}],"stream":true}'
```
They see 502 after ~8s and connection resets in client.
Sofia: :eyes: Is this only for streaming? Any increased 4xx/auth errors?
Emma: Only streaming so far. Non-streaming generation seems fine. Auth success rates look normal in metrics but auth latency spiked briefly around 09:09-09:12.
Nate: I pulled envoy logs from the frontdoor for that tenant window. Multiple upstream 502s with: `upstream reset before response completed` and `connection queue full` messages. Also saw `max_concurrent_streams` exceeded on some midproxy hops.
Sofia: That points at HTTP/2 stream saturation or keepalive/connpool issues between edge -> midproxy -> auth/proxy. Any recent deploy touching auth cache or headers?
Emma: Customer said we rolled token-introspection change at 08:55. deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-18T08:54:12Z ID: deploy-9182 rolled auth-cache TTL patch.
deploy-bot: Rollout: auth-service config patch (auth-cache ttl=0 temporarily) -> 20% -> 100% at 08:58 UTC.
Raj: TTL=0 would disable local caching and cause auth-service to hammer redis/backends for each request. If auth becomes slow, edge can backlog streams waiting on auth. That could saturate connection windows and produce 502s.
Nate: Confirmed high auth-service p99 latency from 08:56-09:11 in APM (~700-900ms) and redis connection pool churning. Edge kept requests open waiting which exploded concurrent streams.
Sofia: Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback the config (re-enable cache), 2) throttle streaming for that tenant, 3) add short-circuit fallback to non-streaming model variant. What's easiest now?
Emma: I triggered a rollback of deploy-9182 at 09:18. Noted customer still seeing errors during rollback window. I asked Support to enable tenant fallback as temporary safety.
Raj: While rollback propagates, we can also patch envoy to increase `max_concurrent_streams` and bump upstream connpool size for midproxy for that host, but that's riskier. Prefer rollback first.
Nate: After rollback starting 09:18:30 we saw auth p99 drop back to ~120ms by 09:20 and 502 rate for that tenant drop ~85% by 09:22. Client confirmed partial recovery.
Emma: Customer says success rate improved. They want root cause and repro steps to prevent recurrence.
Sofia: RCA notes: auth-cache TTL set to 0 removed local hits -> auth backend surge -> increased auth latency -> edge streaming requests queued -> HTTP/2 stream max reached -> upstream resets -> 502. Contributing: long streaming sessions keep streams open and are sensitive to auth backpressure.
Emma: Action items:
- [SRE] add a canary check in deploy job that verifies auth cache TTL not set to 0 for global config (Raj)
- [Infra] make `max_concurrent_streams` and connpool autoscaling more lenient for streaming tenant bursts (Nate)
- [Product] add per-tenant streaming throttle fallback flag so Support can disable streaming quickly for escalations (Emma)
- [Support] notify customer of mitigations and request logs for any residual failures (Emma)
Raj: Quick repro we used for smoke: 50 parallel curl streams with --limit-rate to keep payloads streaming -> watch envoy `downstream_cx_total` and `upstream_reset` lines. Sharing script in thread.
Emma: Leaving customer on monitoring. Closing once no errors for 60m. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
